Al-Bahar Medical Services
supplies professional hospital equipment, surgical tools, and homecare nursing support, but
does not manufacture or sell consumer continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), smartwatches, or wearable trackers
. For personal health tracking, these consumer and clinical devices operate via distinct mechanisms.
Al Bahar Medical Services
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs)
How it works:
A tiny sensor goes under your skin to measure sugar in fluid.
Usage:
Sends real-time numbers to a phone or reader.
Examples:
FreeStyle Libre and Dexcom.
Cureus
Smartwatches & Wearable ECGs
How it works:
Uses light sensors (PPG) and electrical pads (ECG) on the wrist.
Usage:
Checks heart rate and looks for irregular rhythms like atrial fibrillation.
Note:
Wrist-based blood sugar features on consumer watches are still experimental and not medical-grade.
American Heart Association Journals
Sleep Trackers & Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)
How it works:
Uses movement sensors and heart data during rest.
Usage:
Sends vital signs securely to doctors to manage ongoing health from home.
